name: Antenna Length Calculator
blurb: quarter-wave antenna length and keep-out for a frequency
intro: Gives the starting length of a quarter-wave (or half-wave, 5/8, loop) antenna from λ = c/f: for wire with 0.95 end-effect shortening, for a PCB trace as a range between air and the thick-laminate limit εeff ≈ (εr+1)/2, with a start length at the long end to trim down. Also the copper keep-out and ground plane that application notes recommend.

inputs.label: Laminate εr
inputs.help: For PCB traces; FR-4 ≈ 4.4 at 2.4 GHz.

usage: Give the frequency in Hz (engineering notation: 433.92M, 2.44G), the antenna type (quarter, half, fiveeighths, loop) and how it is made (wire, pcb with εr, or custom velocity factor). It returns the free-space wavelength, the length to cut in mm (for pcb also the expected resonant range), the copper keep-out and the ground-plane size, and a table for common ISM bands. Use it for the first cut of a wire whip or PCB trace antenna before tuning with a VNA.
sources: λ = c/f; 0.95 end-effect shortening for wire antennas: ARRL Antenna Book, chapter 2
PCB trace εeff ≈ (εr+1)/2 and keep-out practice: TI AN043 'Small Size 2.4 GHz PCB antenna' and DN007
Keep-out λ/20 and λ/4 ground plane: rule of thumb from chip-antenna application notes
